messages:
maria: Heads up — customer hitting break on go get after we republished a tagged v2 release. They see 410/404 from proxy and 'missing go.mod' style errors. Can we triage?
nik: Ugh. Do we have the exact error output they pasted? Also GONOSUMDB/GOPRIVATE settings?
maria: Pasted from customer: 
```
$ go get github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go@v2.0.0
go: github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go@v2.0.0: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/@v/v2.0.0.info: 410 Gone
```
They also tried direct `GOPROXY=direct` and got 404 from our git host for the tag.
oliver: That usually means tag moved/republished with a different commit or the v2 module path isn't present in the repo at that tag (go expects module path to include /v2). Did the release include go.mod with module path `github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/v2`?
maria: I checked the tag on our mirror: tag exists but go.mod there still says `module github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go` (no /v2). Looks like the tag was republished from an older branch without the v2 module path change.
devon: Classic mismatch — consumers using semantic import versioning fail when the module path and tag versions are inconsistent. Workarounds: 1) re-tag with updated go.mod that uses /v2, 2) publish a v1-compatible tag (drop v2), or 3) instruct customers to `require github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go v2.0.0` with a replace pointing to a commit.
maria: Customer is on tight timeline, wants a short-term client-side fix. They can do `replace` but many downstream projects don't want to patch. Any auth/caching gotchas?
nik: If you republish tags, GOPROXY cache can still serve old refs. Recommend invalidating proxy cache if possible (for our hosting) and ask customers to `GOPROXY=direct go get ...` to hit git host. But if tag points to the wrong commit there's no fix without republishing.
support-arch: For immediate mitigation, provide this snippet customers can add to their go.mod to fetch by commit: 
```
require github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go v0.0.0-00010101000000-abcdef123456
replace github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go => github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go v0.0.0-00010101000000-abcdef123456
```
They need the pseudo-version for the commit that contains the v2 module path change.
devon: Also confirm whether their environment blocks direct git access (enterprise firewalls) — that could explain proxy vs direct differences.
maria: Repro steps I ran: 
1) git ls-remote --tags origin | grep v2.0.0 -> shows tag hash `abcdef1`
2) git checkout abcdef1 && cat go.mod -> `module github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go`
3) go env -> GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
So tag points to pre-module-path-change commit.
nik: OK. Action items:
- oliver: can you confirm whether we accidentally republished the v2 tag from the wrong branch and if we can force-update? :eyes:
- devops (assign): check whether our git host will allow tag rewrite and whether that will break existing customers.
- maria: share the pseudo-version of the correct commit with customer as temporary workaround.
oliver: I looked — someone pushed v2.0.0 tag from a CI rollback branch to restore a build, and that branch didn't have the /v2 module path change. We can either create a new v2.0.1 with correct go.mod or re-tag v2.0.0 (risky). Recommend publish v2.0.1 and add note in release.
maria: I'll relay v2.0.1 plan to the customer. Any notes about go.sum / proxy invalidation?
ik: If we publish v2.0.1, proxies will pick it up fine. For customers still referencing v2.0.0 they'll need to switch. If we re-tag v2.0.0, the proxy caches may still serve the old metadata; re-tagging is messy.
support-arch: Also add docs snippet for SDK consumers: when module uses /v2 ensure import path uses `/v2` and tag is semver-major. Include quick repro steps for support tickets.
maria: Sending customer the short-term pseudo-version workaround and ETA for v2.0.1 release. Escalating to eng-oncall if we decide to re-tag. Ticket #INC-2026 opened. :thumbsup:
